summary: Intermittent 429s on SSE streams during nightly background flush after VPC egress NAT port exhaustion
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on Private (VPC) report opaque 429 responses for long-lived SSE streams during our nightly background flush/housekeeping window. The customer observed this recurring between 03:00-03:30 PDT after migrating their dedicated pool to the new VPC egress path.

Impact:
- Several real-time dashboards (SSE) saw spike of 500+ 429s over a 20m window, impacting DataBeam users' streaming sessions.
- Background flush jobs (bulk small requests) complete successfully, but concurrent SSE clients are intermittently rejected with 429 until the egress NAT state stabilizes.

Environment:
- Deployment: Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC) on dedicated GPU pool
- Region: prod-us-west
- Customer tier: private
- Components: sidecar egress, NAT gateway, cluster sidecar health probes, rate-limiter, serving runtime

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1. Cron background flush starts (many short-lived HTTP/1.1 POSTs from workers to /v1/embeddings) at 03:00 PDT.
2. Workers create many ephemeral outbound TCP connections; connections close quickly on completion.
3. Concurrently, several SSE streams (long-lived) from same customer remain active.
4. Within 10-15 minutes, SSE clients receive 429s; console shows "rate limit exceeded" headers but token accounting in console still shows available quota.

Observed behavior:
- 429s report on SSE responses with X-RateLimit-Remaining headers inconsistent with console readout.
- Edge logs show many ephemeral source ports reusing NAT mapping; origin sees many connections from same egress IP but different source ports.
- Sidecar metrics show high short-lived connection churn and ephemeral-port exhaustion warnings in nginx sidecar logs.

Expected behavior:
- Background flush traffic should not cause long-lived SSE streams to receive 429s (quota separation & smoothing should prevent this).

Relevant logs / snippets:
- nginx-sidecar: "[warn] worker 2: ephemeral port highwater 6143/65535"
- rate-limiter: "token-accounting: route=sse tenant=T-DBA short_requests=1200 long_requests=24"
- edge: "nat: conn_reuse=0 ephemeral_port_runout=true"

Notes on customer config:
- Customer uses a managed NAT gateway with 1 elastic IP for egress.
- They recently switched sidecar egress to route via a new NAT path as part of VPC migration.
- Background flush workers are configured as a cron and perform hundreds of concurrent short connections per minute.

Why this is unique / hypothesis:
- We believe the root cause is not classic token-bucket accounting but operational port exhaustion and proxy affinity changes that cause connection churn to appear as many distinct short sessions at the edge. The rate-limiter interprets the sudden influx of short requests (from the same tenant but new source ports) as increased concurrency for quota windows, triggering 429s for coexisting SSE streams.

Immediate customer-facing workaround suggested:
- Stagger background flush jobs to reduce concurrent short-lived connections (splay cron schedule).
- Move background flush workers through a different egress IP / NAT pool if available.
- Temporarily raise burst pool for the tenant via console (if enterprise controls allow).

Longer-term actions proposed (see investigation_notes):
comments: 2026-03-12 03:40 - Maya Chen (Support): Initial triage with customer, asked for sidecar and NAT logs and timestamps. Customer confirms migrations on 2026-03-10.

2026-03-12 04:10 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Reproduced ephemeral-port warnings on internal staging by running parallel short-connection workers; observed same nginx warning and transient rate-limiter spike.
2026-03-12 07:22 - Priya Nair (Solutions): Provided customer with splay guidance and a short-term cron-schedule template to reduce parallelism during 02:50-03:40 window.
2026-03-12 11:05 - Customer (DataBeam): Applied splay and reported reduced 429s in the next maintenance window; still saw a small set of rejections for a few users.
2026-03-12 15:00 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Opened related PRs to add edge-side ephemeral-port metrics and expose NAT pool saturation in the console (see related_github_prs).
investigation_notes: Confirmed correlation between cron start times and 429 spike windows using request traces from 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-12.

Reproduced with synthetic worker that opened 1200 short connections over 5 minutes from a single egress IP; rate-limiter transiently increased concurrency buckets and then produced rejections for long-poll routes.

Hypothesis: NAT ephemeral port exhaustion + lack of per-ingress-path quota separation causes short-lived connection fanout to be attributed in the tenant's concurrency accounting, affecting SSE routes.

Sidecar nginx config currently reuses source ports but NAT path is configured with single elastic IP; need to evaluate whether connection reuse at the sidecar level can be improved or whether NAT pool size must be increased.
Console currently visible metrics do not include NAT ephemeral port utilization; this made root-cause harder to identify.
next_steps: Action: Recommend customer splay background jobs (done) and add alternate NAT IP for background workers (customer action).
Action: SRE to add ephemeral-port saturation alert to prod sidecars and to expose a NAT-utilization dashboard for private deployments (ticket INT-4421 created).

Action: Engineering to update rate-limiter to prefer route-based quota segregation so long-lived SSE routes are exempt from short-request burst accounting (PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/902).
Action: Product to evaluate console UX for showing egress NAT metrics and a recommended splay template for customers on private VPCs.
resolution: Workarounds applied: customer staggered background flush and provisioned an additional NAT egress IP, which eliminated the bulk of 429s for subsequent windows. Engineering will deploy a rate-limiter patch in the next sprint to better separate short-lived request bursts from long-lived SSE concurrency accounting. Monitoring and an alert for ephemeral-port saturation will be added to Private runbooks. Follow-up: verify patch in canary and schedule a postmortem runbook entry.
postmortem_followup: Create a runbook entry for Private customers describing NAT sizing and splay best practices.
Add an automated recommendation banner in Console when Private deployment exhibits >50% ephemeral port utilization during any 30m window.
Track rollout of rate-limiter route segregation change and validate with DataBeam in staging.
